project.title: Performance and mechanisms of sodium percarbonate enhancing volatile fatty acids production from food waste anaerobic fermentation: Focus on protein transformation
project.description: The conversion of food waste (FW) into volatile fatty acids (VFAs) via anaerobic fermentation is typically limited by substrate hydrolysis and acidogenesis. This study investigated the potential mechanisms of sodium percarbonate (SPC) pretreatment in enhancing anaerobic fermentation of FW, with a particular focus on protein transformation. The results showed that maximum VFA production reached 16,624.31 mg chemical oxygen demand (COD)/L at an optimal SPC dosage of 240 mg/g total suspended solids (TSS), representing a 98.8% increase compared to the control group (8,361.31 mg COD/L). SPC pretreatment accelerated FW solubilization, enhanced the biodegradability of the released organic matter, and enriched populations of hydrolytic and acidogenic microorganisms. Metagenomic sequencing and amino acid concentration profiling revealed that SPC significantly accelerated the conversion of protein hydrolysates. Specifically, SPC stimulated the expression of chemotaxis and transport genes (cheBR, pct, and amiABC), thereby enhancing the cellular uptake of amino acids and oligopeptides. Furthermore, SPC pretreatment increased genes associated with amino acid conversion to VFAs via the Stickland pathway, promoting highly efficient biotransformation. These findings demonstrate that SPC pretreatment is a highly effective strategy for overcoming metabolic bottlenecks, offering a promising approach for enhanced resource recovery from food waste.
